To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Taken together, the departures would cap, time-bar and disclose away most of our protection, including for title and fraud, while leaving three known cash and value leakages unresolved: Riverlark, the DD-005 bonuses and Bluefen. Nothing in it is cleared for acceptance.

## 1. Threshold point: the "market context" and "FINAL" framing

The preamble says these terms are "standard and widely accepted," were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," and are "FINAL." We should not give that framing any weight.

- **This is counterparty assertion, not our authority.** Under playbook sec 0.4 and 6.3, only our own authority process can confirm a position. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback. Nothing in our record shows that anything was settled at principal level.
- **"Market standard" is not a reason to move.** Our positions stand on their own merits.
- **Recommended response:** Tell Seller counsel in writing that we do not accept that any position is agreed or final, and that all points remain open pending our mark-up.

## 2. Issue-by-issue departures

### A. Liability architecture

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | **Reject.** 20% matches our conditional fallback, but that fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. A number matching a fallback does not clear it, particularly when it arrives packaged with heavily adverse terms elsewhere. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** Five times our position. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar | **Reject on both size and mechanism.** At five times our figure plus a deductible structure, the first AUD 250k of loss is effectively self-insured by us. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months | **Reject.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. |
| **Fundamental / Title** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject firmly.** "Administrative simplicity" is no justification. Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. |
| **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)** | Universal default | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Reject. This is a hidden override.** It would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants under the general cap, basket and time bar unless we carve each one out. The default should run the other way. |
| **Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)** | No carve-outs | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | **Reject. Highest priority.** As drafted, it could be argued to shield the Seller's own fraud. The carve-out is not negotiable and no one on our side may waive it. |
| **Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"** | Settled | OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | **Reject the characterisation.** We have not agreed this. Tax and IP stay open as separate categories. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

- **General disclosure (DL 1.1 and 1.2).** The letter discloses the entire data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." This is exactly the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure the playbook rejects. Combined with the knowledge bar below, it could neutralise most warranties. We should:
  - delete 1.1 and 1.2;
  - limit disclosure to specific matters fairly disclosed in the letter, with enough detail for us to assess their nature and scope; and
  - state that the data room is not deemed disclosed.
- **Non-admission clause (DL 1.4).** This is broadly acceptable as a non-admission, but it must not dilute specific disclosure. Add: "without prejudice to the Buyer's rights under any specific indemnity."
- **Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew *or could discover* from the data room or public records. That is a blanket exclusion and an indirect second route to general disclosure. **Delete it.**
  - If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to the actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
  - Note that the Seller's own letter puts DD-004/DD-005/DD-006 matters in front of us. Under cl 8.3, that knowledge alone would bar claims on exactly the issues we most need protecting. That is why those matters need specific indemnities or price mechanics rather than warranties.

### C. Conditions and completion mechanics

**Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3): reject.** The Seller's summary says the consent is "addressed." Its own Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue, so it is a material customer.

The Seller's mechanism has two problems:
- "reasonable endeavours" alone is insufficient for a consent this material; and
- treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery" of the consent letter ignores the cl 11.3 conditions.

We should require an effective written consent *and* evidence that its conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion that only we can waive.

**Riverlark (cl 2 / 7): reject.** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, there is a change-control clause (8.1), and the facility is not repaid (DL item 3). A release "following Completion" means we close on an encumbered company. We require:
- a current payout letter;
- direct repayment from Completion funds, as part of debt-free/cash-free; and
- executed security releases and discharges delivered at Completion, plus PPSR releases where relevant.

A post-Completion release would be acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark *and* Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

**DD-005 bonuses and funds flow: reject.** The Seller calls the AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller" but does not itemise it. Because the bonuses are triggered by Completion, the Company pays them, so in practice they would be borne by us after Completion. DL item 5 also flags that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed. We require one of:
- a specific funds-flow line item deducted from price as Debt, including all triggered on-costs; or
- a Seller-funded payment, backed by an indemnity covering bonuses, on-costs and any related claims.

### D. Specific risk items

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): reject the "adequate" position.** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. Our concern is wider: ownership and transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials under DD-004 cl 7.3, plus any third-party IP claims. We should:
- broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership, transfer and infringement losses connected to Ironquay;
- keep the SOW3 cure, meaning cleared payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable; and
- make the indemnity sit outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

Note that the AUD 180k open balance (DD-010) is not independently verified in either direction. We should not assume it is owed or that it has been paid. Require bank-verified evidence.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6): reject "not expected to be material."** That is a Seller conclusion with no basis. The Seller's own letter (item 6) says scope, access and any notification duty are undetermined and the investigation is preliminary. We should equally *not* assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any loss figure. We should require:
- preservation of all logs and evidence;
- a completed investigation;
- regular written updates and pre-Completion access to findings;
- conduct-of-matter rights; and
- a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, including regulatory, notification and third-party costs if they eventuate.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k): do not accept either label yet.** The Seller says these are "ordinary-course," but its own letter (item 8) says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. These are three related renewals of AUD 110k each, read together, which suggests possible splitting. We should:
- assess timing, terminability, accrual and related-party aspects;
- treat them neither automatically as Debt nor as a price deduction; and
- reserve treatment pending diligence, with a specific warranty or indemnity as an option.

**Title (DD-012): insufficient.** The internal share register is a document the Seller supplied, not independent proof. The letter (item 10) concedes we have not verified it. We require independent evidence:
- ASIC company extract and searches;
- share issue and transfer history;
- PPSR searches for encumbrances over the shares;
- Seller board approval and authority documents; and
- title and capacity warranties in the fundamental regime.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** These are lower priority, and the letter's characterisation is plausible: a notification obligation only, and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. We should still verify both against the full documents ourselves (change-of-control wording, definitions of "assignment") and diarise the lease notification as a Completion deliverable.

### E. Staleness of the Disclosure Letter

The letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**. It is now 5 November 2026. Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 may all have moved on.

- Require a brought-down Disclosure Letter at signing.
- Require no general disclosure at Completion.
- Treat any update as a factual assertion to be verified, not as a cure.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing** in writing. Nothing is settled, and no fallback has been authorised.
2. **Liability:** restore a 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket and a 24-month claims period. Do not offer 20% or 18 months without Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft.
3. **Fraud carve-out:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
4. **Fundamental regime:** title and capacity at a 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.
5. **Delete the cl 12.3 "applies to all Claims" override.** Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, payment and covenants as separate categories. Tax and IP remain open.
6. **Disclosure:** strike the general disclosures in DL 1.1 and 1.2. Specific fair disclosure only. Require a refreshed letter.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Any fallback limited to named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and never applied to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** an effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions, as a CP before Completion.
9. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and releases delivered at Completion.
10. **DD-005 bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as an explicit funds-flow item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180k independently.
12. **DD-006:** evidence preservation, investigation, updates and a specific indemnity. No assumption of breach or immateriality.
13. **Sandbar:** diligence first. No automatic Debt or price treatment either way.
14. **Title:** independent ASIC, PPSR and authority evidence beyond DD-012.

**Escalation note:** If the deal team wants to explore the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks as a trade for, say, a clean fraud carve-out and a proper fundamental regime, that decision belongs to Amelia Frost. It needs her prior written authority referencing this draft before anything is signalled to the Seller.
